parakeet: Because escaping a cult is only half the mission. Building communities worth belonging to is the other half. So let's start with the definition of a cult. A cult is any system of power and belonging that uses coercive control, enforced conformity, and dependency to preserve authority at the expense of individual autonomy. Cultic structures can appear in religion, politics, business, culture, and relationships, and are marked not by what they believe, but by how they control. Cults use the same playbook no matter the setting. Authority that cannot be questioned, truth that cannot be challenged, belonging that depends on obedience, fear, guilt, or shame to keep people in line, and of course, that exploitation of time, money, or devotion that only benefits a few at the top. The difference between a cult and a healthy community is simple. Healthy communities give you room to think, choose, and grow. Cults demand you conform, obey, and surrender. So when I say I'm anti-cult, I mean I'm against any structure, religious, political, corporate, or cultural, that uses coercive control to strip people of their freedom, autonomy, or dignity. Because we don't just need to escape cults, we need to build communities worth belonging to. So let's talk about the core elements of cult dynamics. We'll start with authoritarian leadership. This is a central figure or ideology that claims unquestionable authority. Loyalty to the leader or ideology outweighs loyalty to the truth or personal well being. There's also absolute truth claims. The group asserts exclusive access to truth, salvation, safety, or success. Doubt or dissent is reframed as betrayal, weakness, or sin.
